claims.text: The investigated material is an equiatomic CoCrFeNiCu nanoparticle alloy containing 1 at.% Mn.
The nanoparticles are synthesized by inert gas condensation.
Thermal stability in this system is governed by differences among elemental segregation energies.
Mn has a lower segregation enthalpy than the elements that remain uniformly distributed.
Above a critical temperature, low-segregation-enthalpy species such as Mn migrate preferentially to the nanoparticle surface.
Elements with higher segregation enthalpies remain uniformly distributed during heating.
Segregation-enthalpy differences cause preferential outward diffusion of Mn during heating.
Preferential surface diffusion of Mn disrupts the homogeneous alloy structure.
Mn segregation leads to localized phase separation or compositional inhomogeneity.
The resulting phase separation or compositional inhomogeneity affects catalytic and thermoelectric performance.
Above an onset temperature, the Mn surface concentration will increase relative to the baseline.
Other elements having low segregation energies will also become surface-enriched.
Measured segregation behavior will agree with DFT-derived segregation-energy predictions.
Surface segregation will correlate with changes in catalytic activity.
Surface segregation may be accompanied by morphological changes indicative of destabilization.
The proposed mechanism applies to CoCrFeNiCu nanoparticles over catalytic temperatures of 773–1173 K and thermoelectric temperatures of 473–1923 K.
Extreme oxidation can dominate and invalidate segregation-enthalpy-controlled behavior.
DFT can be used to calculate element-specific segregation energies, while high-temperature XPS and atom probe tomography can test the corresponding surface enrichment.

contradictions.description: The claimed boundary extends thermoelectric applicability to 1923 K, but the proposed experiment and falsification test stop at 1173 K, so the upper 750 K of the stated applicability range is not tested.
